analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only: docs/reference/prediction-decision-telemetry.md (head lines 3 and 29-43) and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (patch hunk near base line 578). I examined the changes against the threat model.

prediction-decision-telemetry.md adds an explanation of how projected_service_us relates to projected_prefill_tokens and projected_decode_tokens. It covers per-batch-step decode charging, the smoothed MeasuredDecodeStep rate, and MTP decode-depth capping. It states that wire fields are unchanged. The text adds no new fields, secrets, prompts or token IDs, and it grants no authorization. It does not touch TB-011 (App Attest authorization) or T-053/T-054. The doc explicitly says the telemetry does not alter provider acceptance policy or billing.

protocol-messages.md clarifies that sample_age_ms in performance_measurements is elapsed time since the newest observation, applied per workload bucket and per current-posture series in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.observe. It also says completed samples keep the receipt-order EWMA and sample counts. This describes producer-side telemetry semantics only. These values are measurement-only and non-routing in the existing doc, so there is no new trust boundary and no new attack surface. The coordinator-side consumption of out-of-order or stale samples (the clamp and freshness logic in the platform repository) is outside the supplied evidence. I have no evidence that the age-semantics change affects any security decision, and the doc still describes the telemetry as untrusted provider input.

No regression is identified. The cited Swift source files were not supplied, so the documentation claims about their behavior are unverified. That is a coverage limit, not a finding.
